Nique Clifford.text: Justin Martinez: Asked Mark Daigneault about newly-acquired guard Nique Clifford: “The first thing I like is not about his game. It’s him as a guy. He’s a really, really good guy. He’s a team guy. He wants to be a part of team basketball. He wants to compete. He’s willing to earn what he gets. He’s got all of the marks of the makeup that we look for, which I think Sam (Presti) has done a great job of as we’ve layered guys in through the draft or through trade. He tries to find people who naturally align with the way that we want to be, and he does that. And I think that’s important when you have a team that has the ethos that we have established at this point.“And then as a player, there’s just a versatility to him, I think. I think he’s a guy who can defend different positions. He’s good on the ball and he’s good off the ball. He’s sound on the principles on that end of the floor. And then on offense, he can play in a system, I think. We’ll see as we go, but he seems to be a guy who can fit into what we want to do as just a plug-in guy.And, also, he’s got some secondary creation stuff that he’s shown flashes of in his career so far. He’s got a little bit of a body of work, but that’s in a different place in a different context. So, as usual, we’re gonna stay open-minded and throw him out there. He’ll declare where he’s at. He’ll do some things well, and he’ll need to pick some other things up. We’ll meet him where he is and just start trying to help him get better inside of our stuff.”x.com

Ayo Dosunmu.text: Ayo Dosunmu: I know I came here at the trade deadline last year as a “wait and see.” That’s what the whole league was saying. I’m a basketball junkie, so I knew the deal. When you get traded, it’s like a breakup. Except in basketball, you can’t pick your new girl! You don’t know how it’s gonna go! Might be a good fit, might not be. Thank God, from the first day, everybody embraced me here. I got on the plane to Minnesota with 2 bags, and I literally just kept those two bags all through the playoff run. My fiancée was texting me like, “Are you sure you don’t want me to bring you some new clothes?” But I was so locked in that I didn’t even want to think about anything but ball. I had spent my entire life in Chicago, in my cocoon with my family, all the way from a kid to Illinois to the Bulls. So it felt like God was telling me, “Alright, it’s time to grow up. I’m throwing you in the deep end for the first time. You gotta ADAPT or sink.”The Players' Tribune
